t: Charge Q is given a displacement r=aî+bĵ in an electric field E⃗=E₁î+E₂ĵ The work done is

The electrostatic force acting on a charge Q in an electric field is given by:
F⃗ = Q E⃗ = Q(E₁î + E₂ĵ)

Work done (W) is the scalar (dot) product of force and displacement:
W = F⃗ · r⃗ = Q(E⃗ · r⃗)
W = Q(E₁î + E₂ĵ) · (aî + bĵ)
W = Q(E₁a + E₂b)

Concept: Work done is a scalar quantity determined by the dot product of the force and displacement vectors, where î·î = 1, ĵ·ĵ = 1, and î·ĵ = 0.

Correct Answer: (A) Q(E₁a+E₂b)

t: The electric field intensity just sufficient to balance the earth’s gravitational attraction on an electron will be (given mass and charge of an electron respectively are 9.1×10⁻³¹kg and 1.6×10⁻¹⁹C )
s:
To balance the downward gravitational force on an electron, the upward electric force must equal its weight in magnitude:
|F_e| = F_g
|q|E = mg
E = mg / |q|

Taking g = 9.8 m/s²:
E = (9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 9.8 m/s²) / (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) = 5.57 × 10⁻¹¹ N/C ≈ 5.6 × 10⁻¹¹ N/C

Since the electron has a negative charge, the electric force is opposite to the direction of the electric field. To produce an upward force, the electric field must act vertically downward, giving E = −5.6 × 10⁻¹¹ N/C.

Options (B), (C), and (D) are incorrect due to calculation errors in applying the mass-to-charge ratio with g.

Correct Answer: (A) −5.6×10⁻¹¹N/C

t: Two plane polarized light waves combine at a certain point whose electric field components are E₁=E₀Sinωt E₂=E₀Sin(ωt+π/3) Find the amplitude of the resultant wave.
s:
To find the amplitude of the resultant wave for the given electric field components, we use the formula for the resultant amplitude of two combining waves. These components are: E₁=E₀sinωt
E₂=E₀sin(ωt+π/3)
The general formula for the amplitude E of two superimposed waves E₁ and E₂ with a phase difference is: E=√(E₁²+E₂²+2E₁E₂cosϕ)
where ϕ is the phase difference between the two waves. In this scenario, ϕ=π/3.
Substituting the given expressions and phase difference into the formula, we get: E=√((E₀)²+(E₀)²+2(E₀)(E₀)cos(π/3))
Given that cos(π/3)=1/2, this simplifies to:
E=√(2E₀²+E₀²)=√3E₀
Thus, the amplitude of the resultant wave is √3E₀≈1.73E₀
